title: At the End of the Way

content.text:
## At the End of the Way

_by San Jaya Prime & Kan Men Caban Ix'Lamat_

My oldest written work in this lifetime, and while I'd accepted, embraced, and became the entity "Jaya" since the 90s, this was part of the process in accepting who I am as "Kan", as well. Written in my personal Abedic script, as well as where the script itself is defined, the entire book exists within the bounds of a single Composition notebook.

Written between late 1999 and the spring of 2004, the book is divided between an alchemical study on the materia and structure of the multiverse, as well as an exploration on the nature of light and time, going into short stories, then ending on the poems I wrote in triptych form -- "The Wayfarer's Song" . . with excerpts from many of those appearing in my "[Spectral Iteration](spectral-iteration)" fractal art book, as well as on Instagram, and of course in songs such as in our "[Warriors in Waiting](warriors-in-waiting-live-set)" live set.

There was a brief period of a few months when Kan showed interest in the world of humans, and in that time a few small portions from the book appeared on DeviantArt ([link](https://www.deviantart.com/lamatkan)). That, however, will likely be the only external source of publication. It remains a work that is intimately connected to the paper that it was written on.

It is mentioned here due to its connection to all other works. My spirit family and inner circle have read and had access to the book itself. That is enough for me.

Music, sound, sights, writings... . all ties back to this single work. Fitting, then, that the opening words of the book are:

_<font face="Times New Roman">In a single work my world defined that one could measure the depth of mind.</font>_

This work itself is the advent of [The Infinity Paradox](all-that-is) and the greater war against entropy itself. While many of my actions on this world may be seen as amoral, they are in fact rooted in the scope of a much larger race... and the clock's ticking.

texts: "Tick, tock. Tick, tock. Always running out of time. Yours is almost used up. You're between seconds, lost in the infinite possibilities between tick and tock. Tick, you're alive. Tock.. Well, it was a good life, but a short one. Tick, tock, tick, tock, tick..."
